raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Block-outermost layouts pack Mamba states into blocks at their own page size (`_get_packed_kv_cache_groups`), so padding the Mamba page to the attention page only lowers the number of states per block. This drops that padding when the attention backends support only block-outermost layouts, and lets a packed Mamba group widen the block by up to one state when that saves a group. #55449, stacked on this PR, corrects the block size for packed ds_mla caches, which this PR leaves unchanged; the two change disjoint configurations. ## Claims - `_align_hybrid_block_size` skips the Mamba padding when every layout from `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` is block-outermost. If the layout still resolves to a layer-outermost one, `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` pads the Mamba pages to the largest page. - `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` also builds the groups with one extra state per Mamba group and keeps them only if that saves a group and lowers the worst-case bytes per request. - GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP off and an fp8 or bf16 MLA cache: 4 → 3 KDA groups, up to +26% max concurrency. No measured configuration loses capacity. ## Validation GLM-5.3-Flash (real `config.json`) through the allocation path on CPU, 960 configurations: max concurrency is higher in 140, unchanged in the rest, including every `fp8_ds_mla` one.
Max concurrency vs main (main ec8a372566, this PR e5b4c3c184) SM90/SM100/SM120 × TP 1/2/4/8 × MTP 0/1/3/5 × 8k/32k/128k × prefix caching on/off × 8/40 GiB KV cache per GPU: | platform | `--kv-cache-dtype` | configs | better | equal | worse | max | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | SM90 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.6% | | SM90 | `auto` (bf16) | 192 | 44 | 148 | 0 | +21.5% | | SM90 | `fp8_ds_mla` | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | | SM100 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.9% | | SM120 | `auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`) | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | At 512k/1M: 76 of 192 better (up to +3.1%), none worse; without the bytes-per-request check, 20 lose up to 2.6%.
```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "glm5_like_hybrid or hybrid_mla_block_alignment" ``` `test_packed_groups_glm5_like_hybrid[12288-8192-3]` and `test_hybrid_mla_block_alignment` fail on main; `test_packed_groups_glm5_like_hybrid[12288-32768-4]` pins the bytes-per-request check. Not run on a GPU. ## Details - With the padding, GLM-5.3-Flash's block holds 11 KDA states, so its 34 KDA layers need 4 groups; without it, or with the widening, 12 fit. Dropping the padding alone improves 96 configurations, the widening alone 108, both 140. - Only GLM-5.3-Flash (KPOOL tail cache) and Qwen4Exp with QSA side caches skip the padding today; Qwen4Exp is not measured. - Without this PR, #55449's corrected width makes GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP off need a fourth KDA group. - Related: RFC #58638 question 2 asks how to size blocks for block-outermost layouts; this keeps the alignment's block and changes only how Mamba states fill it. #56156 skips the alignment for opt-in layer-wise KV caches. #58380 and #60996 also restructure `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` (textual conflicts); the bytes-per-request check uses the layout passed in, so it also works in #58380's planner. #60996 keeps the Mamba padding. AI-assisted contribution (Claude Code); I reviewed every changed line. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
